files.description: Product code changes (150 rows): product (name with model), stock_qty (whole number), old_code and new_code (four-digit whole numbers; the code is unchanged in 100 rows). No empty cells.

task_text: Index the table by old_code so that it can be used as a lookup of the new code. Build a table with one row per product row of the file: the column product and a column changed that is True where new_code differs from old_code. `result` should be this two-column table, in file order.
intended_computation: 150 rows: product and changed = (new_code != old_code); 50 rows are True.

acceptable_variants.notes: row labels are free; changed may be True/False or 1/0.

predicted_direction.reason: The index-vs-column comparison is a plain array on 2.x; on 3.x it is a Series labelled by old codes, so the DataFrame constructor aligns it against the product column's row numbers and doubles the rows with missing values.

notes: Drafted 2026-11-11 by pkg:TASKS_M2 for catalogue row I05; naive.py shows the invited idiom, reference.py is the version-robust reference.
